containerViews.name: Containers: dev-skills plugin

componentViews.name: Components: skill definitions
componentViews.description: Component diagram for the skill-definition container — one box per skill, grouped into the ten functional areas by dashed boundaries. Rows read as invocation distance from the user: entry points, the feature chain, secondary workflows, helpers, then what they write to. Thirty boxes is over the readable target and deliberately so: every skill is a real unit and collapsing any of them would hide it. Connectors stay hidden until you pick a box.

decisions.q: Where does the system boundary sit?
decisions.choice: One software system: the dev-skills plugin as installed.
decisions.why: Single repo, single owner, everything ships together — the ownership and deployment-alignment heuristic (c4-model.md 2.2).

decisions.q: Which containers earn a component view?
decisions.why: It is the only container with internal structure worth decomposing; C4 5.1 warns component views are the fastest to rot.

decisions.q: Container or component: an individual skill?
decisions.choice: Component — one box per skill, all twenty-two.
decisions.why: A skill is not separately deployable — it is loaded into the agent's context — so the deployability test (2.4) makes it a component. A hook script or a python script runs as its own process, so each is a container.

decisions.q: How are the twenty-two skills grouped?
decisions.choice: Ten dashed boundary rectangles; the groups are not elements.
decisions.why: A functional group is an organisational grouping, not an abstraction level (2.6, 11). Collapsing each group into a single component would hide every skill and put a fifth level in by the back door.
They are read at runtime and are not code inside another process; C4 2.3 admits a file store as a container.
No broker, queue or topic appears anywhere in the plugin.

decisions.q: Is the usage-report script a container?
decisions.why: It is executed as its own system-python process rather than loaded into another unit, so the deployability test (2.4) puts it beside the hook script.

decisions.q: How are the four files the plugin writes under the Claude config directory modelled?
decisions.choice: One external data-store system, renamed 'Claude config store'.
decisions.why: Lesson logs, eval scores, the run-usage log and the per-skill customisation files are four files in one real location; four boundary boxes would be four views of the same store (2.3, 11).

decisions.q: Where do the three skills added since the last run sit?
decisions.choice: usage-report joins Internal helpers, skill-customize joins Reflection (renamed 'Reflection & customisation'), set-herdr-label gets its own 'Workspace' boundary.
decisions.why: All three groupings are ones CLAUDE.md already uses to describe the skill set, so the boundaries stay real rather than invented (2.6).

decisions.q: Which new external systems cross the boundary?
decisions.choice: herdr, Claude Artifacts, the git remote and documentation MCP servers.
decisions.why: Each is reached by a named skill and cited to it, and each is modelled at the boundary only, never its internals (11).
